messages:
jen: heads-up — since we flipped the new kernel-routing heuristic last night I’m seeing transient GPU OOMs on a few hosts. logs point to large KV cache fragmentation + sudden drop in prefix hit-rate.
ivan: confirmed. our internal metric shows prefix_cache_hitrate dropped from ~76% -> ~48% for the 20:00-22:00 window. memory usage stayed high on GPU side despite lower request rate.
maya: probably the kernel path changed so we’re not coalescing small prefix keys the same way. batching changed too?
jen: batching policy switched to aggressive batching for mid-length requests which may increase KV key churn. also the kernel selector started routing shorter contexts to the new fast-kernel, which doesn’t use the compact cache layout.
sam: quick profiling output I ran: 
```
# sample
hotkeys: 42% of hits are dominated by top-10 prefixes
avg_seq_len_before: 128
avg_seq_len_after: 96
gpu_mem_frag: +12%
kernel_path_switch_ratio: 0.24
```
dana: interesting — top-10 prefixes dominating means our prefix normalization might be keying variants separately (whitespace, punctuation). that would tank hit-rate when a subtle kernel change emits a slightly different key.
jen: agree. proposed immediate mitigations: 1) softcap on GPU cache with probabilistic eviction, 2) normalize prefix keying (trim/normalize whitespace + stable hashing), 3) revert the new kernel-routing for Canary until we confirm.
ivan: +1 on normalization. i have a quick normalizer patch that canonicalizes whitespace and lowercases for non-tokenized prompts. should be very low risk.
maya: re: softcap — we can implement a soft watermark that signals the prefetcher to slow down and convert LRU to probabilistic eviction under pressure. config suggestion: 
```
cache:
  key_normalizer: "whitespace_collapse|lowercase_if_ascii"
  soft_cap_bytes: 11500000000
  hard_cap_bytes: 12800000000
  eviction_policy: "probabilistic_lru"
  ttl_ms: 600000
  sliding_ttl: true
```
jen: can someone run a quick A/B on Canary with normalizer + softcap? target: measure prefix_hitrate, kernel_path_switch_ratio, and OOM count over 4h window.
sam: running profiler + tracer now: `./profiler --model=v2 --sample=2000 --out=/tmp/trace.json` will dump kernel path per request.
dana: also add a tiny sampling to log full raw prefix -> normalized key mapping for top N prefixes. helps verify normalization correctness.
ivan: note — if normalization reduces entropy too much we might get cold-hot hotspots and increased fragmentation. need to pair normalization with a TTL bump + probabilistic prefilling.
maya: alternative approach: make kernel routing aware of cache layout. if fast-kernel can request compact KV layout or use an adapter that maps its produced keys to the canonical namespace. avoids double-caching.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollback if OOMs > 2 in 30m.
jen: timeline: ivan deploys normalizer + softcap to Canary in ~15m. sam will collect profiler traces. if metrics look good by EOD we can promote and tweak TTLs.
ivan: pushing patch now. patch notes: "kv: canonicalize prefix keys, add soft_cap + probabilistic_lru; expose stats prefix_normalized_ratio and cache_eviction_sampling"
sam: trace started. initial 10k requests show prefix_normalized_ratio ~0.82 (ie 18% keys changed by normalizer), hitrate jumped +14% on first pass.
dana: promising. keep an eye on latency for fast-kernel path — if normalization causes extra hashing or normalization CPU we might shift latency tail.
jen: thanks all. if we still see OOMs after canary we’ll run fragmentation compaction on the affected hosts + consider temporary throttling of aggressive prefetch.
ivan: if anyone wants the patch: https://git.internal/r/kv-normalizer diff. simple ~120 LOC.
maya: also added a small dashboard: /dashboards/eng-runtime/prefix-cache/normalizer-canary to track relevant metrics.
jen: :thumbsup: good run. follow-up items: 1) validate normalization edge cases 2) rehearse compact-reclaim procedure 3) schedule a perf regression run against the old kernel selector to quantify improvements.
ops-bot: canary monitor configured. will alert if any of the thresholds breach.
jen: closing loop here once we have 4h of data. thanks everyone.
